q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT b1.beer, b1.min_price AS price, s.bar FROM (SELECT s.beer, MIN(s.price) AS min_price FROM serves AS s GROUP BY s.beer) AS b1 LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b1.beer = s.beer AND b1.min_price = s.price FULL OUTER JOIN beer AS b ON b1.beer = b.name ORDER BY b1.beer, b1.min_price, b.name

counterexample: INSERT INTO beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('BeerA', 'BrewerX'); INSERT INTO bar (name, address) VALUES ('BarY', 'AddressY');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the difference in the join order and the use of FULL OUTER JOIN in Q2, which can lead to different results when there are NULL values in the joined tables.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include a beer that is not served by any bar in the 'serves' table, and a bar that does not serve any beer. This will trigger the difference in results between Q1 and Q2.
